claim:bm-v1-stage1-modulus-remodelling.proposition: A coarse-grained collagen IV network (two-bead rods, stochastic NC1/7S crosslinks, no excluded volume) run through the spec's stage-1 protocol — stretch, hold, then switch the chemistry on — yields a separable elastic modulus and remodelling (stress-relaxation) time on real LAMMPS.

pass_if.note: crosslinks decay 46→3; stress drops in the correct direction

claim:bm-v2-stress-vs-strainrate.proposition: Imposing an equibiaxial in-plane strain rate ε̇ on the growing collagen IV network and reading the steady-state stress σ(ε̇) gives the effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ (viscous at slow rates) and the rate at which the response turns elastic — the σ(ε̇) relation a vertex model needs.

claim:bm-v3-junction-bending-rigidity.proposition: This study originally explained the soft modulus as a central-force rigidity-percolation effect (z ≤ 3 < 4). The released code is not a central-force network — it sets junction angles (NC1 at 180° with stiffness 4.0, 7S at 155° and 60°) — so that explanation does not describe the published model, which carries those angles and is still soft (≈0.03 Pa). What this connectivity sweep actually shows is that with angles off (our earlier transcription) and the corrected parameters, the network is sub-isostatic (z tops out at ≈2.0) and soft — a property of the angle-off transcription, not of the paper.

claim:bm-v4-junction-bending.proposition: Junction bending is a released feature (an NC1 angle of stiffness 4.0 at 180°, plus 7S angles), not a new ingredient; how it is applied decides whether it gives a usable modulus. Pinning as-formed restraints on after assembly is ill-conditioned — the sign flips and no reproducible value emerges. Creating real harmonic angles as the crosslinks form, so the network equilibrates with them active (matching the released bond/react templates), gives a positive, well-conditioned, reproducible modulus. The released model is not floppy once its angles are active; its modulus is finite and strongly density-dependent.

pass_if.note: |E| jumps orders of magnitude above floppy
IQR < 0.5·|median| — met by the real-angle path

claim:bm-v5-porosity-bundling.proposition: Of the two geometric readouts the model should reproduce, one is met and one is not. The simulated pore-size distribution reaches the measured corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density, while the protomers-per-strand distribution stays near 1, below the measured 5-7. The released NC1/7S topology has no lateral-association bond, so it cannot form multi-protomer strands — a limitation identified in advance.

claim:bm-r1-published-tissue-baseline.proposition: The homogeneous prism model recovers the paper's confinement regimes: a fixed-volume cell grows TALL under a stiff, slowly-relaxing basement membrane and SPREADS flat under a soft, fast-relaxing one, with cell height rising monotonically along both the BM stiffness and the BM relaxation axes of the Figure 1G map.
claim:bm-r1-published-tissue-baseline.hypothesis: Reimplementing the paper's fixed-volume prism / surface-tension tissue model with a viscoelastic BM reproduces Figure 1G's four stiffness-relaxation regimes and the 1H-J confinement trajectories, with the regime boundary set by the ratio of BM relaxation time to doubling time.

pass_if.note: height non-decreasing along the stiffness axis for all 4 relaxation columns
height non-decreasing along the relaxation axis for all 5 stiffness rows

claim:bm-r2-collagen-network-rheology.proposition: The faithful collagen IV network assembles and carries in-plane stress under staged growth loading on real LAMMPS, and -- on a dense, multi-seed network (300 rods, authors' density 3.0, 12-sigma slab, 4 seeds) -- its macroscopic stress-relaxation time tau rises monotonically with collagen residence time (37 LJ at residence 12.5 up to ~102 LJ at residence 200), reproducing the DIRECTION of Barrientos Figure 2E across the full turnover range. tau carries an intrinsic network-relaxation floor (~37 LJ) at fast turnover and becomes residence-dominated above residence ~50; the elastic modulus is turnover-independent (3.19 LJ), as elasticity should be.

pass_if.note: tau finite at residence 100; NaN at residence 50/25
median tau non-decreasing as residence rises 12.5 -> 200; modulus ~constant

claim:bm-r3-network-expansion-supply.proposition: With a material-insertion process added to the collagen IV network, the composite now expresses all THREE Barrientos Fig 2B-C supply modes and reproduces their ordering: under growth (expansion), remodeling WITH insertion sustains and grows the crosslinked network, remodeling WITHOUT insertion cannot replace diluted material, and a frozen (no-remodeling) network is static and dilutes most. The ordering holds strictly across rod count, crosslink count, and crosslink-per-area density, and is robust across 3 seeds.
claim:bm-r3-network-expansion-supply.hypothesis: Adding a material-insertion process lets the collagen IV composite express all three Fig 2B-C supply modes, and under growth their connectivity orders remodeling-with-insertion > remodeling-without-insertion > no-remodeling.

claim:bm-r4-coupled-2d-epithelium.proposition: The explicit 2D epithelial sheet relaxes under the Tyssue vertex model and yields finite, uniform per-cell geometry: all 12 cell-faces carry the same basal area (5.0) and the same explicit cell height (1.93), and stepping the EulerSolver keeps that geometry finite. The figure-level comparison of this spatial confinement to the homogeneous R1 baseline, and the explicit BM-traction coupling, are not yet in the composite.

pass_if.note: all 12 face areas finite and > 0; min == max == 5.0
per-cell area and height finite and positive after 5 Euler steps (dt 0.01)
stiff height 0.905 > free height 0.700; stiff area 1.105 < free area 1.428
realized area 1.000, BM stress 0.0 under mode=none

claim:bm-r5-explicit-3d-confinement.proposition: The explicit 3D epithelial monolayer runs over the Tyssue engine and per-cell heights and volumes emerge directly from the apical/lateral/basal surface energies and volume targets -- no thin-prism approximation: 206 cells with finite, positive volumes (0.58-1.16) and a monolayer z-extent of ~1.0. The no-BM / elastic-BM / relaxing-BM controls the morphology comparison needs are not yet in the composite.

pass_if.note: Nc > 0 and all 206 cell volumes finite and > 0 (0.58-1.16)
per-cell area and volume finite and positive after 5 Euler steps (dt 0.01)
stiff basal area 1.108 < free 1.198; stiff stress 0.140 > free 0.0

claim:bm-r6-perlecan-growth-perturbation.proposition: Carrying an inferred collagen IV lifetime through BM relaxation to cell shape reproduces the paper's Figure 7 perlecan intervention ordering: perlecan knockdown (loss) gives the TALLEST cells, control intermediate, and perlecan overexpression (gain) the SHORTEST -- with the inferred relaxation time (turnover) kept distinct from the predicted cell height (mechanics). This followed a correction: the figure review caught that the model's perlecan direction was inverted; an audit against the paper (perlecan OVEREXPRESSION shortens the collagen IV lifetime ~1 h vs ~20 h control, knockdown lengthens it ~500 h; "perlecan promotes bond breakage") fixed the perlecan_factor -> lifetime mapping, after which the ordering matches.
claim:bm-r6-perlecan-growth-perturbation.hypothesis: Propagating inferred collagen lifetime distributions for control, perlecan gain/loss and growth-rate changes through the relaxation->shape chain reproduces the relative cell- morphology ordering and uncertainty of Figure 7, keeping inferred and independently predicted outcomes distinct.

pass_if.note: height(loss) > height(control) > height(gain) -- the paper's direction
inferred_relaxation = 5.0 x perlecan_factor; strictly increasing in perlecan

claim:bm-e1-actomyosin-cortex.proposition: A coarse actomyosin cortex carries a cortical tension that rises monotonically with the myosin-contractility proxy, giving a tunable active tension that can be mapped onto the vertex model's cortical-energy parameter.
claim:bm-e1-actomyosin-cortex.hypothesis: A 2D cell-sized coarse filament/crosslink/motor LAMMPS patch produces a tunable active tension and a strain response/relaxation that map onto Tyssue cortical-energy parameters, so the effective cortical term can be replaced by explicit actin without changing the measured confinement in the overlap regime.

claim:bm-e2-actin-adhesion-collagen.proposition: An active cortex transmits force through reversible basal linkers to a collagen membrane patch; the transmitted traction equals linker occupancy times cortical tension (by construction, exactly), the BM strain rate is proportional to that traction, and occupancy rises toward saturation -- so the cortex -> linker -> BM force transfer is occupancy-gated.
claim:bm-e2-actin-adhesion-collagen.hypothesis: Coupling an active cortex to reversible basal linkers and a collagen-IV BM patch produces a traction, linker occupancy and network deformation whose relative relaxation is set jointly by linker off-rate and crosslink turnover, measurable on a single-cell patch before multicellular coupling.

claim:bm-e3-closed-3d-lumenoid.proposition: A closed 3D lumenoid runs over the Tyssue engine: 78 cells enclose a single lumen, per-cell volumes emerge finite and positive (0.50-3.43), and a basal surface (78 faces, area 202.5) is exposed as the basement-membrane coupling shell with a readable enclosed lumen volume (261.7). The lumen-pressure trajectory and the explicit BM attachment / curvature-dependent shape are the next readouts, not yet dynamic results.

pass_if.note: Nc > 0 and Nf > 0 and all 78 cell volumes finite and > 0 (0.50-3.43)
per-cell area and volume finite and positive after 5 Euler steps (dt 0.01)

claim:bm-e4-feedback-predictions.proposition: The epithelium and its collagen basement membrane are coupled both ways: the growing basal surface stretches the membrane and the membrane's stress pushes back on the cells as a basal tension. On the reduced-order (effective) BM path the bidirectional loop runs end-to-end, the three coupling controls (two-way / one-way / uncoupled) behave exactly as the mechanism demands, and subcycling the BM relaxation converges. The EXPLICIT-LAMMPS-collagen-BM path now also runs the real bidirectional loop with correct feedback directionality (two-way feeds a non-zero basal tension back, one-way does not), closing E4's main gap. It reveals two honest departures from the effective-BM path: the explicit collagen carries intrinsic bond-virial stress (so the reduced "uncoupled bm_sigma==0" inert control does not transfer), and its subcycling DIVERGES rather than converges -- so the explicit loop is stable only in a bounded regime (~40 rods, coarse subcycling), and a stable explicit-BM subcycling integrator + gain calibration are the open items.
claim:bm-e4-feedback-predictions.hypothesis: With one-way, uncoupled and uniform-material controls, the fully coupled system predicts regimes - growth-driven turnover, spatial BM heterogeneity, contractility-dependent confinement, partial adhesion/network failure - in which cell height and lumenoid growth depart measurably from the paper's homogeneous, one-way predictions.

pass_if.note: two-way realized 1.006 and one-way/uncoupled 0.767 both < preferred 1.150; mode-dependent
bm_sigma stays O(1-40), no blow-up at 40 rods/16 steps (120 rods/24 steps diverges)

narrative.question: How does collagen IV molecular turnover set basement-membrane (BM) stress relaxation, and how do BM mechanics, epithelial growth and actomyosin mechanics jointly determine epithelial cell height and lumenoid morphology? (The original v1 sub-question — the effective modulus E(ε̇) and remodelling time τ(ε̇) a growing boundary produces, the two numbers the AICS vertex model couples to — is the P0/P1 reproduction core this campaign now builds on.)

decisions.title: Growth as preferred-vs-realized (2026-10-20): RESOLVED in direction — the first deliverable is now the two-way experiment where a PREFERRED geometry grows (division OFF) and the realized geometry emerges/lags under BM reaction (R4/R5/E4). Open: calibrate the stiffness/relaxation vs preferred-growth-timescale mapping and run the full BM control matrix.

Growth vs division (2026-10-20): RESOLVED for the MVP — growth is a preferred-geometry ramp with proliferation OFF; the paper's proliferation stays a separate faithful-reproduction extension. Confirm with the expert that no-division growth is the right MVP scope.

Explicit-LAMMPS coupling as a separate gate (2026-10-20): RESOLVED as policy — the explicit-BM path is a separate verification gate (numerically delicate, E4 F5), marked apart from the reduced-order primary results; stabilizing its subcycling is the open engineering item.

Perlecan direction (R6): RESOLVED — verified against the paper (perlecan promotes collagen IV bond breakage; overexpression ~1 h, control ~20 h, knockdown ~500 h lifetime) and the perlecan_factor mapping was inverted so R6 reproduces Fig 7. Left here as a sanity-check item for the expert to confirm the reading.

Lumen geometry vs model-side elasticity (2026-10-20): keep the new lumen geometry/volume (a geometry class computing enclosed volume) SEPARATE from model-side lumen elasticity/pressure; start E3/E4 from an already-closed lumen (no nucleation). Osmotic water-pumping is a later branch.
Reproduction conventions: the article alone does not fix every convention needed to reproduce it. Acquire the supplemental tissue-model equations and the precise Figure 1 parameter values.

Released turnover kinetics: pin down the grand-canonical monomer exchange, the distance-gated breaking, the 7S-specific mechanics, and the original stress-to-energy conversion before freezing the collagen reference.
Collagen supply law: a fixed concentration (for reproducing the paper) or a secretion flux (for the lumenoid hypothesis). Decide per study.
3D calibration data: obtain lumenoid geometry over time, cell height and volume, membrane thickness, and collagen-versus-laminin staining before calibrating the 3D models.
Actin fidelity: use a validated reduced cortical model unless a molecularly-resolved actin cortex changes a measurable prediction. An explicit go/no-go call.

Composite modularity: keep the collagen-network composites as thin selections over one general, parameterized network builder (chemistry, bending stiffness, density, and strain protocol as configuration), rather than near-duplicate generators.

Absolute modulus in pascals: the angle-stabilized model reproduces the published ≈0.03 Pa and gives a reproducible modulus in reduced units (E ≈ 3 LJ). An exact value in pascals additionally needs the released monomer exchange, the distance-gated 7S break (0.95), and the dense starting configuration — or accept the reduced-unit value and settle the energy-scale choice below.
Engine for the early stages: LAMMPS now, with Smoldyn revisited when surface binders are added.
Energy scale: report the modulus in pascals (fit to a measured modulus) or keep kT units and report a ratio.
Coupling contract: which vertex-model term receives the membrane — a basal tension, a mobility, or an elastic spring.
Linker values: density, spring constant, and off-rate; sweep the off-rate as a multiple of the crosslink break rate.
Growth rate: extract ε̇ from the lumenoid radius over time (still needed).
Slab thickness and layer count (one z-stack away).
Which readout calibrates and which validates: the remodelling time calibrates the formation probability and the time unit, so it cannot also validate.
